frames.review_note: The correction works. v02 changes Nagoji's horse from v01's black horse with a white blaze to a bay: red-brown coat, black mane and forelock, no blaze or star. The lower legs are cropped out of frame. The rest of the image is unchanged, and the edit added no new faults. Nagoji still has the moustache, the clean-shaven chin, the rust turban, sleeves down and boots. Ibrahim matches his sheet, and Padmini is in her cream sari with no blouse. One small flaw is in both versions: Nagoji's visible ear shows no gold stud. It is tiny at this panel width, but a retouch could add a flush gold dot to the lobe. Older composition points the correction did not touch: Nagoji rides on the viewer's left, about level with Padmini rather than slightly behind her left side, and Padmini's side-saddle seat cannot be confirmed. The caption fits easily in the open grey sky at the top right.

v04 is clean. In v03 the bay horse had a white stripe down its forehead. In v04 it is gone, and the head now reads as solid ochre red-brown bay with a black mane, a dark muzzle and no white markings. At 5x zoom I found no seam, smear or tonal patch. A pixel diff shows the edit re-rendered a feathered rectangle of about x 442-788, y 299-647 (the horse, Nagoji's legs and sword, part of Padmini's walking stick, the hind legs of Ibrahim's horse). Outside the stripe, the changes are only tiny texture and tone differences (low-frequency shift of 12/255 or less). At 3x zoom there is no visible structural change and no hard edge at the boundary. Nagoji's face (x 580-680, y 180-300) is pixel-identical, with his curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and gold ear stud. The contact sheet at /tmp/claude-501/ch9rv2-sheets/page-01-panel-02.png did not exist, so I compared the two frame files directly. The single CAPTION fits in the misty sky at the top centre or top left.

The correction works. v02 changes Nagoji's horse from v01's near-black horse with a white blaze to a bay: red-brown coat and black mane, with no blaze, star or snip, even at full zoom. The changes stay on the horse and add no new faults. Nagoji matches his sheet: rust turban, a tiny flush gold stud, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, sleeves to the wrist, the red sash, a talwar and boots. Padmini wears the cream sari in the old drape with no blouse, gold at her throat and wrists, the stick strapped along the saddle and the sword at her side. She looks ahead without turning, as the script asks. One older point the correction did not touch: white gate pillars stand behind the riders, although 1.2 already has them out on the road. Read it as a second gate. The three balloons fit in the open sky between and above the two heads, and the empty road in the centre gives more room.

The fix is done. Padmini is still mounted and alone, in profile, chin lifted toward the road with the faintest smile. There is no guard and no gate. She matches her sheet: lined face, thick black hair coiled at the nape (a few grey highlight strands, as on the sheet), gold ball earring, gold bead necklace and bangle, cream-and-gold sari over her left shoulder with the right shoulder bare, and the leather-wrapped sword hilt at her right hip. Her hand on the reins is sound. Her brown horse with the white blaze matches 1.1. The walking stick is out of frame, which is acceptable. The bright daylight follows on from the morning in 1.2. A large empty sky at upper right holds both balloons clear of her face.

Acceptable. A low red laterite wall circles tiled Kerala roofs and broad trees, with no towers or bastions. The gate stands wide open and is broad enough for carts. Two bare-chested Nair guards with high topknots, no turbans, white mundu at about knee length, spears and small round shields watch toward the viewer. No riders are in frame. There is no fort, no European building and no text, and the brass standing lamps on the verandah are traditional. Minor: the mundu hang just to the knee rather than visibly hitched, and the light is bright midday like 1.3 and 1.4. Clear blue sky top left of centre has room for the caption.

The correction works. Nagoji's horse is now Kayal: a red-brown bay with a black mane and no white markings. Its lower legs are out of frame. The edit swapped the coats, so Padmini's horse is now black with a white blaze. That matches her black horse with a star in 2.2, so page 2 is now consistent. It still differs from page 1, where Padmini rides a brown horse with a blaze. Padmini's mount is not locked in the bible, so this is minor. Nagoji is unchanged: tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, clean-shaven chin, sleeves down, plain brown boots. Padmini wears the cream sari with no blouse. The guard bows toward the riders. There is no text or anachronism, and open sky at upper centre for the guard's and Padmini's balloons. v01 is not acceptable because Nagoji rides a black horse with a blaze.

The correction works and adds no new fault. Nagoji's horse on the left is now a red-brown bay much closer to Kayal's sheet: black mane, no white markings on the visible head, lower legs out of frame. In v01 it was a duller dark brown. Nothing else changed. The black horse with a small star is Padmini's: she stands beside it with her hand on its saddle, matching her mount in 2.1 v02. The black horse's lowered head is steeply foreshortened but readable, as accepted before. Nagoji is half-dismounted in period wrapped boots, with a flush gold stud, clean-shaven chin and sleeves down. Padmini holds her stick and wears the cream sari with no blouse. The clerk with palm leaves and stylus and the swordsman match the script. There is no text. Padmini's balloons go on the roof tiles and sky above her (upper centre).

Hard checks pass: Nagoji's ear is a tiny flush stud with nothing hanging, chin clean-shaven (faint shadow only), sleeves down to the wrists, Padmini's hair thick, black and coiled at the nape, Kerala setting, no text. Boots are out of frame in this close shot. The beat reads: Nagoji is deadpan and Padmini flashes a toothy grin with her stick in hand. Minor: Padmini's sword is at her left hip, not her right. Clear sky at the upper centre for both balloons.

The correction fixes the boots. v01 had modern lace-up boots with eyelets, laces and lug-type soles. In v02 they are soft brown mid-calf boots bound with wrapped leather thongs, with no eyelets or laces and thin flat soles, matching his sheet. They stand side by side on the stone ledge by the step. The edit touched only the boots. Nagoji is barefoot and cross-legged with a tiny flush gold stud, clean-shaven chin and sleeves down. Padmini wears the cream drape with no blouse, her stick laid along the mat. Lamplit drummer shadows show through the inner doorway. Small existing quirks carried over from v01: a second brass tumbler on the mat, and a bindi on Padmini not seen in 2.1 or 2.2. The plain white wall at upper centre takes Padmini's balloon, and the sky at upper left or the stone step at the bottom takes the caption. v01 is not acceptable because of the modern boots.

Hard checks pass: Nagoji's ear is a tiny flush stud with nothing hanging, chin clean-shaven, barefoot, sleeves down to the wrists, seated on a woven mat, Kerala verandah, no text. Revathi appears only as bare feet with a gold anklet and an indigo-and-gold hem stepping onto the stone, which matches the script. Minor: Nagoji is drawn sharp, not out of focus, and glances back over his shoulder with the tumbler at his lips. This stretch of verandah has a dark wooden turned pillar where 2.4 had square granite pillars. Padmini is out of frame. Both captions fit on the large plain floor at the bottom or in the sky at the upper centre.

Clean on every hard check. Nagoji has a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, a clean-shaven chin (only light stipple shading on the jaw), sleeves down to the wrists and his commander dress. His feet are out of frame, so barefoot cannot be seen, but no boots show either. Revathi matches her sheet: bare right shoulder with the sari end over her left, flat gold coin necklace, armlets, anklet, jasmine braid, sandalwood line and kohl, no tali. The sari is the sheet's royal blue rather than a darker indigo. Kerala verandah, no text, hands sound. Lettering space: the caption fits the top-left door lintel or the open floor at bottom left, and Revathi's balloon fits over the pillar and trees in the upper centre.

Acceptable, with two small acting and prop differences. (1) Revathi's bow is deeper than the script's 'smallest fraction of a head': her head is lowered and her eyes are downcast, so it reads slightly more deferential than Padmini's lean. It still reads as a mutual bow. (2) Padmini holds her sheathed sword (brass pommel, leather-wrapped grip) in her right hand instead of wearing it at her right side. This is consistent with the script's sword. Hard checks pass: Padmini's hair is thick and black, coiled at the nape, with no grey. Her sari is cream with a gold border as on her sheet, and she has her walking stick. Revathi has her bare right shoulder, armlets, jasmine braid and sandalwood line. The necklace is oval gold pieces, close enough to coins. Kerala pillared verandah (reverse angle of 3.1), no text, hands sound. Padmini's two balloons fit over the sky and palms at top left and the plain central pillar.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Hard checks pass. Nagoji is not drawn here, only a blurred foreground fragment. The setting is a Kerala verandah with grey granite pillars, a tiled-roof courtyard and an open-wick brass lamp, which matches page 3. Revathi sits on a woven mat, and there is no text, chair, fort or ship. Minor points: (1) The out-of-focus cream fragment at lower right, with a gold stripe, a red patch and a soft hand, is ambiguous. It reads as Nagoji's knee and hand, or as Padmini, and if it is a seated Nagoji it slightly contradicts 4.3, where he is still standing. (2) Revathi is already seated before 4.3's 'settling onto the mat' beat, though this is consistent with the picked 3.3. (3) Her necklace is round gold beads rather than flat coins, which matches her sheet but not the bible line. Lettering space: wall above her head and sky between the pillars at upper right.

Clean. This is a tight close-up on the mouth with a faint, not-quite smile. It has the flat gold coin necklace, the jasmine braid, the armlets and the sari over her LEFT shoulder, with her RIGHT shoulder bare. The background is the same granite-pillared verandah with an open-wick brass lamp. There is no text. Lettering space: the plain wall and doorway at upper right, plus the strip at upper left. The second, short balloon can also sit low on the sari without touching the face.

The correction works. In v01 the servant wore a stitched red short-sleeved blouse under her drape. In v02 she wears a plain off-white old Kerala drape over one shoulder with bare arms and no blouse. Her hands and the brass plate placement are still sound. A pixel diff shows the edit stayed in the servant's area, apart from a small redraw of Revathi's face, which now has the sandalwood line at her hairline that the bible asks for. Nagoji is the same as in v01: tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, sleeves down to the wrists, barefoot, talwar at his side. Padmini's cream sari and the stick across her knees are unchanged. Revathi still matches her sheet (indigo and gold, bead necklace, jasmine braid, armlets, right shoulder bare). No text, anachronism or new anatomy fault. The script beat holds: Nagoji standing at frame left, his empty mat in front of him, Revathi gesturing from her mat, and the servant setting the plate by her knee while she ignores it. Revathi's line can go on the plain cream wall at upper right or in the sky at top centre, clear of all faces.

Hard checks pass. Nagoji's ear ornament is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging. His chin is clean-shaven, his moustache thick and curled, and his sleeves are down to the wrists. He sits cross-legged and barefoot on a mat facing Revathi, who is on her own mat, also level. Padmini, with black hair coiled at the nape, her stick and her sword at her side, walks away through the inner doorway. The lamp has an open wick, and there is no text, chair, fort or ship. Hands and feet are sound. Minor points: (1) Padmini exits at background centre rather than directly behind Nagoji. (2) The pillars are round wooden columns, not the grey granite of 4.1 and 4.2, so there is slight setting drift. (3) Revathi, at right, speaks first. Her balloon can sit on the plain wall at top right or across the top centre, with Nagoji's below it at upper left over the sky and roof.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Clean on every hard check: seated on a woven mat, Kerala stone verandah with a tiled-roof courtyard, no text, plain hair parting, indigo-and-gold sari over the LEFT shoulder with the RIGHT shoulder bare, coin necklace, armlets, anklet, jasmine braid and sandalwood line all present. The untouched brass plate of rice and side dishes matches 4.3. Minor: she leans a little on her planted right hand, so her spine is not quite 'straight'. She looks toward frame right, so the NAGOJI (off) tail goes to the right edge. Lettering space: the open sky at upper right and the plain wall behind her head.

Shows the beat: his right hand pushes the cream sleeve up past the elbow of the bared left forearm, palm up. The brand is a pale puckered ring of raised ridges about a hand's width above the wrist, with no letters, numerals or cross. The long thin white scar runs from the wrist toward the elbow. Red sash, mat, brass lamp, Kerala verandah, no text. Ear and chin are not in frame, and sleeves are exempt here. Minor: the gripping right forearm at the left edge shows bare skin with no sleeve visible (allowed, since 5.2 is exempt from the sleeve rule), and the ridged nails are hard to see. No face is drawn: put the NAGOJI (off) tail at the top-left edge and the REVATHI (off) tails at the right edge, toward where his arm reaches. Lettering space: the floor and mat in the lower middle, and the pillar and wall at upper right.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Hard checks pass. The ear ornament is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging. The moustache is thick and curled. Sleeves are down to the wrists. He sits on the mat, and his feet are out of frame. Rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash and talwar hilt are correct. The memory bleeds in at the right edge like a stain: a clerk's hand with a quill over an open ledger in a stone cellar under a slit window, with only ruled columns and grey smudges, no letters or numerals. Kerala verandah, no text. Minor: light shadow-stubble texture on the chin and jaw; it still reads as clean-shaven. Minor: he looks toward frame right (into the memory), while Revathi in 5.1 and 5.3 also looks right, so the screen direction between them is loose. Lettering space: the sky and courtyard wall above the middle, and the stone pillar at upper left.

Hard checks pass: seated cross-legged on the woven mat, Kerala verandah and courtyard, no text, correct costume (sari over the LEFT shoulder, RIGHT shoulder bare, coin necklace, armlets, anklet, jasmine braid, sandalwood line). Her narrowed sidelong frown while eating reads as the beat, and the hands are sound. Minor prop drift: she eats a whole peeled banana, and a brass bowl of whole bananas with a brass pot sits beside her, where 5.3 showed a single piece of plantain and 5.1 the rice plate. Minor: the hair parting has a faint orange-brown tone, the same as the accepted page 4 frames and much fainter than the red streak rejected in 5.3. Lettering space: the plain wall at upper middle.

All hard checks pass. Nagoji has a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, a clean chin (only faint texture shading), sleeves to the wrists, bare feet and a mat. Revathi's right shoulder is bare and the sari end is over her left. No text, Kerala setting. Soft notes: (1) Screen direction is flipped against the rest of the scene. Revathi is at frame left and Nagoji at frame right here, but 4.4, 6.5 and 7.2 put Nagoji left and Revathi right. A mirror is not a fix, because it would move her bare shoulder to the wrong side. (2) The pointing finger is medium-sized rather than large in frame, and it touches the step edge in front of her own mat rather than exactly between the two mats. Lettering space: the low-detail red earth and stone step across the bottom, plus the sky and roof gap between the two heads at top centre.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Minor only: her right shoulder sits behind her braid rather than showing clearly bare, but there is no stitched blouse. Her upper back is bare skin and the pallu is over her left shoulder, so the fix holds. There is light hatching on Nagoji's jaw, but his chin still reads clean-shaven. The three balloons should stack in the top band (sky, pillar capitals, back roof, right wall), with the third over Nagoji's cream back if needed. Both heads stay clear.

Clean. Close on Revathi, seated on her mat. A band of shadow crosses her upper face, and she looks away from him with her chin on her hand. Right shoulder bare with an armlet, sari end over the left shoulder, flat gold coin necklace, jasmine braid, sandalwood line. The folded left arm (elbow on knee, hand at chin) is anatomically sound. No text. Kerala setting, consistent with the page. Lettering space: the open sky above the courtyard at upper right, and the low-detail courtyard and stone floor at right and lower left.

All hard checks pass. Nagoji has a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, a clean chin (only faint skin-texture shading on the jaw), sleeves to the wrists, bare feet, and sits on a mat. Revathi sits on a mat with her right shoulder bare. No text. Kerala verandah with no fort or European buildings. It matches the chapter's screen direction (Nagoji left, Revathi right), with a clear space between them. Minor notes: two food plates with brass cups, one per mat, where the script implies the single plate by Revathi's knee (7.3 shows one); no banners are shown (a still bamboo blind stands in); Nagoji's talwar is not visible.

Clean on the hard checks. Revathi matches her sheet and bible row: indigo-and-gold sari over her LEFT shoulder, right shoulder bare, jasmine braid, gold coin necklace, armlets, anklet, sandalwood line, kohl, no tali. She is seated on a mat on the Kerala verandah, her right hand closing on the coins at her throat. Hands are sound. No text. Minor points: the necklace coins read more like rounded beads than flat coins, and the brass vessel in the foreground holds jasmine rather than the food plate that appears in 7.3. Lettering space: plain wall top centre between her head and the pillar for both REVATHI balloons, and clear floor bottom right for the caption.

Clean on the hard checks. Nagoji wears a tiny flush gold ear stud with nothing hanging, a thick curled moustache and a clean chin (only faint skin shading). He has the rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, red sash and cream trousers, and is barefoot and seated cross-legged on the mat, leaning in a little with an open hand. Revathi sits still on the mat with the sari over her left shoulder and her right shoulder bare. Hands are sound. No text, and the verandah, pillars and lit doorway are consistent with 7.1. Minor points: no talwar is visible (plausibly set aside while seated); the two mats read as one long mat; and the brass plate that Revathi pushes aside in 7.3 is not shown between them. Lettering space: trees and roofline top left for NAGOJI, and plain wall top right above Revathi for REVATHI.

Clean on the hard checks. Revathi matches her sheet and bible row (sari over her left shoulder, right shoulder bare, jasmine braid, coin necklace, armlets, anklet, sandalwood line). She sits on a mat and pushes the empty brass plate aside with two fingertips across the verandah stone, which is the script beat. Hands and the bare foot are sound. No text. The setting matches 7.1 (lit doorway at left, red-earth courtyard and tiled roofs at right). Minor point: a small stray pebble sits beside the plate, which is harmless. Lettering space: sky and trees top right, and open stone floor along the bottom.

Clean on the hard checks. A tight head-and-shoulders shot of Revathi with an edged, knowing smile, matching her sheet: jasmine braid, flat gold coin necklace, bell earrings, armlets, sandalwood line, kohl, sari over her left shoulder and right shoulder bare, no tali. The setting matches the page (lit doorway at left, pillars and courtyard at right). No text. Lettering space: sky and foliage top right beside the pillar, and the doorway area top left. Both REVATHI balloons fit without covering her face.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Clean on the hard checks. Ear is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging. Chin is clean-shaven (only faint stipple shading on the jaw). Sleeves are down to the wrists, he is barefoot, cross-legged on a woven mat and setting the brass tumbler down with his eyes on it. Kerala verandah, no text. Minor: the talwar is not shown (plausibly set aside while seated). Lettering fits in the plain white wall left of and above his head and along the dark roof eave at top.

The correction does what it was meant to do. v01 shows plain, smooth, tall riding boots with no thongs, which is not the boot on his sheet, so it is rejected. v02 keeps everything else the same: the shot is still tight and low, the boots sit side by side on the stone verandah step, there is red earth in the courtyard beyond, the daylight matches 9.1, 9.3, 9.4 and 9.5, and there are no figures and no painted text. The boots are now soft, slouched brown leather bound with wrapped leather thongs, knotted with trailing ends. They have no eyelets, no laces and no modern soles, only a stitched welt and a low heel that suit the period. The correction introduced no new fault. One small leftover inconsistency: in 2.4 v02 and 12.1 v02 the boots are shorter, mid-calf, with thongs spiralling down the shaft. Here the shafts are a little taller and the thongs sit in one band near the top, like a garter. The material, colour and wrapped-thong idea are the same, so I think this is acceptable, but it is not an exact match. There is plenty of clear space for Revathi's three off-panel lines: the red courtyard either side of the boots, the strip of sky at the top, and the stone floor and mat along the bottom. Revathi is off-panel on the verandah behind and to the left of the camera, so the tails point to the bottom edge at lower left.

Passes the hard checks. Ear is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging. Moustache is right and the chin has no beard, though there is light stubble shading on the jaw (the bible allows stubble only in captivity, but this reads as shading). Sleeves are down to the wrists, he is barefoot on a mat, jaw tight, looking out at the courtyard. Kerala setting, no text. Minor: (1) the soft-focus brass lamp inside the doorway at far left has a finial that reads like a small cross, which is odd in a Nair house but tiny at print size; (2) the talwar hilt at his hip is a slightly odd double-curved shape, mostly hidden by his arm; (3) the pillars are brown here, against grey stone in 8.1 and 8.2. The large clear sky at upper right holds the caption and the balloon.

Passes the hard checks. Nagoji's ear is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, his chin is clean (faint stubble shading only), sleeves are down to the wrists and he is barefoot. Revathi matches her sheet and bible row: indigo and gold sari over the LEFT shoulder, bare RIGHT shoulder, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, armlets, sandalwood line. Both sit on a mat, no chairs, Kerala verandah, no text. Deviations: (1) the framing is a frontal side-by-side two-shot, not 'from beside Revathi past Nagoji's shoulder'; (2) the inner room shows the seated women themselves in lamplight (heads bent together), not their shadows on a wall; (3) Nagoji also looks toward the doorway; (4) the background women seem to wear sleeved blouses. The beat still reads: Revathi turns toward the lit inner doorway where women sit together. Lettering space is tighter but workable: the stone pillar and sky at top left, the white wall strip between the two figures, or the floor strip at bottom left.

Passes the hard checks. Nagoji's studs (both ears visible) are tiny and flush with nothing hanging. Chin is clean-shaven, sleeves are down to the wrists, he is barefoot on a mat and the talwar is at his hip. The over-the-shoulder shot from behind Revathi is correct: jasmine braid, bare RIGHT shoulder with armlet, the sari covering the left shoulder. Padmini is a small figure far back in the inner doorway with her walking stick, thick black hair coiled at the nape and a listening expression. Kerala setting, no text, hands sound. The large plain white wall in the upper third takes both balloons above the faces. Minor: (1) Padmini's sword hangs at her LEFT side, where the bible says right; (2) she is lit rather than half in shadow; (3) the pillars are dark wood, against grey stone in 8.4. The tail point is at Revathi's jaw beside her ear, because she is seen from behind (her head is listed in faces to keep the jasmine braid clear).

Clean on every hard check: Revathi matches her sheet (indigo and gold sari over the LEFT shoulder, bare RIGHT shoulder, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, armlets, sandalwood line). She sits on a woven mat on a Kerala verandah. No chairs, no text, hands sound. Minor: the framing is a medium close-up rather than tight, and the shrug is understated (the bare right shoulder is slightly raised). Her sideways look to the right keeps her eyes on him. Open sky at the upper right gives room for the one balloon.

Hard checks pass. The ear ornament is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging. Chin clean-shaven (normal shading only). Moustache thick and curled. Barefoot, sleeves at the wrists, sitting cross-legged on a woven mat on the verandah. Kerala setting, no text. Hands and feet sound. Minor: the talwar is not visible (set aside). He gazes off to the right, but on this page Revathi is staged to his left (9.1, 9.3, 8.4), so the off-panel tails go to the left frame edge. Plenty of open sky at the upper right and plain wall above his turban for the caption and the two off-panel balloons.

Hard checks pass. Nagoji has a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, a clean-shaven chin (light shading only), sleeves to the wrists and bare feet. He sits on his mat looking up at her. Revathi matches her sheet: sari over the LEFT shoulder, bare RIGHT shoulder, jasmine braid, coin necklace, armlets, anklet. Her hand at the pleats reads as smoothing the sari. Kerala verandah and courtyard, no text, anatomy sound. Minor: she is already fully upright rather than caught mid-rise. Her head is high in the frame, so the three balloons need to sit in the sky to either side of her head (left sky above the roof, and the sky and pillar tops between x 0.4 and 0.67). There is enough low-detail area for this.

Clean on every hard check. Revathi stands at the threshold of the lamp-lit inner hall, half in its shade, looking back over her bare RIGHT shoulder. The sari pallu hangs from her left side, with jasmine braid, armlets and anklet. Kerala verandah with a red-earth courtyard, no text, feet and hands sound. Minor: the small carved relief bands on the pillar plinth are ornamental and read as carving, not lettering. Large open sky at the upper right and plain white wall beside her take the two balloons easily.

Clean on every hard check: a narrow strip of the empty doorway in shade, with an oil lamp inside, mats on the verandah and the courtyard beyond. No figures and no text (the sunlit patch on the mat is only weave). Same wooden pillars as 9.2. Minor: the single white blossom lies on the wooden threshold board, not on stone, and is drawn a little large and open for jasmine, but it reads clearly as the dropped flower. No lettering needed.

All hard checks pass: the ear ornament is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, the chin is clean-shaven, he is barefoot on a woven mat, his sleeves reach his wrists, Padmini's hair is thick and black, the setting is a Kerala verandah and there is no text. One minor point: Padmini's sari is cream with a gold border, not the script's 'muted earth-toned silk'. That matches her approved sheet and the rest of the page. Lettering space: Padmini's line can sit on the plain wall right of her head (x 0.33-0.48, y 0.0-0.25) and Nagoji's in the sky at the top right.

Padmini's head and eyes turn toward the lamp-lit doorway at the right, which is the script beat. Her hair is thick, black and coiled, and there is no text. The empty mat by the door reads as the one Revathi left. Minor: her sword hangs at her left hip, while the chapter's standing note says right side (it is on her right in 10.1). Her sari is cream and gold as on her sheet. For lettering, the roof beams and sky at the top centre and top left take both balloons clear of her face.

All hard checks pass. The ear stud sits on the lobe with nothing hanging, the chin is clean-shaven, he is barefoot, his sleeves reach his wrists, Padmini's hair is thick and black, the hall is Kerala-style and there is no text. The drummers with sticks at the open side of the hall are mid-beat. The inset shows bare feet on the red earth with the boots on the verandah step behind, as scripted. Minor: Nagoji walks almost level with Padmini, just behind her, rather than clearly following. The drummers wear shoulder cloths. The two captions fit in the sky at the top centre and on the plain red earth at the bottom left.

v03 makes the required fix: Nagoji is small in a tall frame, barefoot on red earth, with the laterite gate behind him (left) and the lamp-lit hall ahead (right). The upper 40% is open sunset sky, with room for all four captions. Turban, cream tunic with sleeves down, red sash, talwar and clean chin all match the bible, and there is no painted text. Remaining fault, accepted for the author list: his ear jewel is a tiny gold bead hanging just below the lobe instead of a flush stud. It is about 3 px at full frame and barely visible at print size. Minor: a small framed rectangle (mirror or niche) on the wall deep inside the hall, too small to matter. v01 and v02 both draw Nagoji large in the foreground, which fails the 'small in a big frame' beat, and both have a visible hanging gold drop.
